attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, endorsed. The linked tweet is a source he cites, but the description of the Act is his.

semantics.note: The draft pulls out the appositive about the Act accurately. It is an evaluative comparison about the present, and it correctly leaves out the separate claims about jeopardy and regulatory capture.

contract.note: The contract correctly says 'closest thing we have' has no ranking standard or set of alternatives. Scoring it would mean adding weights Marcus never supplied, so not_applicable is fair.

evidence.note: The official CAC generative AI measures, published 2023-07-13 with enforcement in Article 21. They show an enforceable alternative existed before the post, but they cannot rank it against the EU draft without an added standard.

reviews.rationale: The claim is an evaluative ranking ('closest thing we have to... real teeth') with no stated measure, set of alternatives, or weighting. The Chinese measures show other enforceable AI rules existed, but they cannot settle the comparison without a standard Marcus did not give. The claim cannot be scored on its own terms.
